correctness.rationale: The gradient computation gives one nondegenerate A1 node; Q=G=0 consists of exactly six transverse F5 points on a smooth conic by gradients and Bezout; explicit inverse blowup proves resolution. Adjunction plus Cauchy bounds each geometric line class and excludes all but six exceptional and fifteen chords; rationality follows from six split base points. Replacing split P1 by one rational node yields \(q^2+6q+1\) and its zeta for all \(q=5^m\). Verification enumerates all 806 rational lines over F5, q=5,25 surface/conic points and 120 group elements; finite tests are only corroboration of the geometric proof.

value.rationale: The characteristic-five Clebsch fiber is singled out in primary classification as an exceptional singular model, so a full arithmetic/geometric description fills a natural gap. The six rational conic points simultaneously explain degeneration of the classical 27-line configuration, all F5-split lines, exceptional six-point S5 action, and every extension-field point count. These results are not merely a cheap singularity or normalization check and have independent use for arithmetic and degeneration studies.
